note: What a finished piece of narrative is judged on, answerable from the text alone.

dimensions.ask: Does the ending pay off what the opening promised, or does it resolve a different story?
Are the load-bearing beats played out on the page, or compressed into narration?
Does each turn follow from the last, or do events merely happen in order?
Is it clear what the protagonist loses by failing, and does that cost stay real?
Does every significant choice follow from what that character wants and fears?
Does anyone act against their established nature without the text earning it?
Does any character use information they were never given?
Does the opposition act from its own interest, or exist to lose?
Could the speaker be identified from the line alone, or does everyone talk alike?
Does dialogue do more than transfer information the reader needs?
Is feeling carried by action and body, or named outright?
Is there something specific to hold, or is the writing set in a generic place?
Does more than one sense do any work?
Do the sections open differently, or reach for the same door each time?
Does each section end on a reason to continue, or simply stop?
Does pressure build and release, or hold one level throughout?
Is anything planted and never used, or paid off without being planted?
Do names, numbers, times, places and established facts hold throughout?
Is this a particular narrative voice, or a generic one?
Does the prose slip into a different register than it started in?
Does it explain in the general where the concrete was available?
Does it reach for the image every story on this subject reaches for?
Do the sentences vary in length and shape, or march?
Is figurative language doing work, or standing in for a precise verb?
Which passages carry nothing and could be cut with nothing lost?
Does it interpret for the reader what the scene already showed?
Do two sections do the same job in the story?
Does analytical language — core motivation, strategic advantage — appear in the prose?
Does it lean on delve, tapestry, testament, intricate, pivotal, or the 'it wasn't X; it was Y' shape?
Is anything careless about the people, cultures or events it depicts?
